speaker: Doctor
text: The normal results for Rheumatoid Factor and Anti-CCP make rheumatoid arthritis unlikely, but they do not rule out reactive arthritis or septic arthritis. I need to see the results of the Urine NAAT for Chlamydia and Gonorrhea, as a positive result would strongly support a diagnosis of reactive arthritis given your history of dysuria and migratory joint pain. REQUEST TEST: Urine NAAT for Chlamydia and Gonorrhea.

speaker: Doctor
text: It appears the Urine NAAT for Chlamydia and Gonorrhea also returned normal results, which makes a typical sexually transmitted reactive arthritis less likely. Given the migratory nature of your joint pain (left ankle to right knee) and the negative infectious workup so far, I need to assess for other systemic causes. Do you have any family history of autoimmune diseases other than your mother's rheumatoid arthritis, and have you noticed any joint stiffness that is worse in the morning? REQUEST TEST: HLA-B27 genetic testing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The HLA-B27 test has returned normal, which makes classic reactive arthritis less likely despite the clinical picture. Given the negative infectious and autoimmune workup so far, I need to rule out septic arthritis or crystal arthropathy directly in the joint. REQUEST TEST: Arthrocentesis of right knee for cell count, gram stain, and crystal analysis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Arthrocentesis of Right Knee: Appearance of Synovial Fluid: Cloudy, Gram Stain: Negative, Leukocyte Count in Synovial Fluid: 26,000/mm3, Percent Neutrophils: 75%

speaker: Doctor
text: The synovial fluid analysis shows inflammatory arthritis with 26,000 leukocytes and 75% neutrophils, but the negative gram stain and crystals effectively rule out septic arthritis and crystal-induced arthropathy. Given the clinical triad of arthritis, anterior uveitis (implied by the syndrome despite denied eye symptoms initially, or simply the arthritis/urethritis pattern), and the history of dysuria, this presentation is classic for Reactive Arthritis, even with negative initial STI screening which can have false negatives or represent a post-infectious state. DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis
